title: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Dec 2026 data)
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos), fetched direct 2026-09-09 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,245 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher. The table headed `2026 release dates` carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `December | Monday, December 28`, alongside the note that `The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT. While we strive to ensure the information is published to our website in a timely manner, we cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online.` 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET (CST in December). The same table's `September | Monday, September 28` and `November | Monday, November 30` rows are the ones this calendar's existing dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 and dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 entries were filed against, so the December row is the same series read from the same primary. Independently consistent with the observed last-Monday-of-month cadence, now validated across 32 consecutive editions whose own mastheads were fetched direct in the same session (Jan-2024 through Aug-2026: every release date is that month's last Monday, the single exception being 2026-05-26, a Tuesday, because Memorial Day fell on the last Monday). Stays estimate on the two limits this lane records: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (no `FED:` prefix covers a District survey page as opposed to a Board release), so this series is structurally unpromotable no matter how good the source is; and this lane never self-confirms. Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, superseding proposals/dallas-fed-mfg-2026-12-28.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28.json
notes: CANONICALIZED 2026-09-09 from the treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 lane's proposal, and the proposal's reason for filing is upheld while the 11-30 sibling's reason for DECLINING to file it is not. The 11-30 ledger declined this row on the ground that 'filing further low rows for a series measured as market-neutral would contradict the finding'; a rule shaped like that removes confounder markers from exactly the sessions where attribution is hardest, which is the opposite of what the calendar is for. The proposing lane filed it because 2026-12-28 is NOT an attributable auction day and this survey at 10:30 ET is one of the reasons. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the missing December member of an established monthly series (dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28, -11-30 already tracked, sibling dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01 tracked), and it sits inside the year's most crowded thin-liquidity session — advance-economic-indicators-2026-12-28 at 08:30, this survey at 10:30, bills at 11:30, treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 and treasury-5y-note-2026-12-28 at 13:00, with fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 two sessions later. That crowding is the exact inverse of the November instance's one distinctive virtue (an empty 08:30 slot), so the attribution test the 11-30 ledger registered does not transfer to this date and this ledger declines to re-register it.
